description: Plan: /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-sc8.57.html, ticket 1. panic stays the one runtime primitive (fz_panic); it takes an exception, which carries a name and a message. Kernel.raise(Name, message) is ordinary fz code that builds the exception and panics with it; raise("text") means RuntimeError, as in Elixir. When fz gets real exceptions, only raise and panic change. The panic prints '** (Name) message' once on stderr and ends the process through the normal exit path, never a signal (today panic dies with exit 132 on run and build); an uncaught failure in the main process exits 1. The interpreter and native share one hook signature; drivers stop reframing (compiler.rs:472-483, aot_shim.rs:624-645, cli.rs frames); Process.exit_fault and fz_exit_fault go. A failing spawned process prints its exception and the others continue (today: silent on a clause miss, whole-program death on panic). Compiler-emitted failures (fz-sc8.63) carry their source location; a raise call's own site is not reported unless raise becomes a macro.
title: raise is a Kernel function over one panic route, and a failure never dies by signal
